result.title: HyperTaxa: Multiscale Genome Representations for Generalized Microbial Taxonomic Inference
result.summary: Reliable microbial taxonomic inference is challenged by the rapid growth of newly sequenced organisms and incomplete reference coverage. While alignment- and database-driven tools remain essential for reference-backed identification, they are not designed for learned inference over species absent from genome-level training. We introduce HyperTaxa, a taxonomy-aligned representation learning framework for open-set microbial taxonomic inference. HyperTaxa encodes whole genomes as multiscale hyperspectral k-mer transition fields and aligns these representations to a taxonomy-derived semantic space using a two-stage Node2Vec-to-MDS procedure that combines local graph structure with global hierarchical distance preservation. The resulting space supports zero-shot inference over species excluded from genome-level training but represented in the taxonomy, generalized zero-shot inference over seen and unseen species, and cascaded genus-to-species prediction. Across benchmark and large-scale disjoint-species evaluations, HyperTaxa improves taxonomic prediction over pseudo-image and transformer-graph baselines, with the strongest gains at higher taxonomic ranks. Ablations further show that multiscale transition encoding and taxonomy-aware alignment are key contributors to generalization. These results position HyperTaxa as a complementary taxonomy-aware representation and candidate-generation framework for microbial identification under incomplete reference coverage and open-set uncertainty.

AI.brief_summary: HyperTaxa 将全基因组编码为多尺度超光谱 k-mer 转换场，并用 Node2Vec→MDS 两阶段把表示对齐到分类学语义空间，以支持零样本与广义零样本的微生物分类推断。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「多尺度编码 + 同时保持局部图结构与全局层级距离」的表示对齐思路，以及面向未见类别的开集泛化评测协议，可能为 LVR 中 latent 表示的几何结构、层级信息保留与未见场景泛化的评价设计提供可核查的类比线索。
